planting.note: Set out a grafted tree in spring once frost danger has passed; this cultivar needs sustained tropical warmth to flower and fruit well.

directions: Mahachanok is a Thai hybrid mango bred in Chiang Mai from a cross of the Sunset and Nang Klanwan varieties, producing an elongated, curved fruit that ripens to a yellow-orange skin with a pink blush. Its seed is unusually long and thin relative to the fruit, giving a high ratio of sweet, fiberless flesh to stone, which is why it is grown commercially in Thailand and marketed abroad under names like 'Banana Mango' for its curved shape. Grow it like other grafted mango cultivars in full sun on well-drained soil, allowing fruit to color fully before harvest for peak sweetness. It has also been trialed as a graft onto established subtropical mango rootstock outside Thailand.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Tropical Research and Education Center — Mango Cultivar Notes

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in a humid, frost-free tropical climate; like other durian cultivars it needs sustained warmth and high humidity to establish and fruit.

directions: Kan Yao is one of Thailand's five major commercial durian cultivars, grown alongside Mon Thong, Chanee, Ruang, and Kradum, and its name (from Thai 'kan,' stalk, and 'yao,' long) refers to the fruit's distinctively long stem. Growers and sellers prize it for holding a longer window during which the flesh is fully sweet while still being comparatively mild-smelling, giving more flexibility at harvest and sale than sharper-smelling cultivars. Cultivate it exactly as other grafted durian trees: deep, fertile, well-drained soil, full sun, and consistent humidity and irrigation, tapering water slightly as fruit nears ripeness to concentrate sweetness. Because it is less widely propagated than Mon Thong, budwood and grafted stock can be harder to source outside Thailand.
sources: Kasetsart University, Faculty of Agriculture — Durian Cultivar Research
Department of Agriculture, Thailand — Durian Variety Records

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in a humid, frost-free tropical climate, following standard durian establishment practices.

directions: Chanthaburi No. 1 is a Thai government breeding program release credited to scientist Songpol Somsri, who by 2007 had crossbred more than ninety durian varieties to produce a cultivar that lacks durian's characteristic strong odor while still bearing rich, flavorful flesh. The reduced smell was developed specifically to ease transport and broaden consumer appeal in markets wary of the fruit's typical pungency. Grow it with the same deep, well-drained, fertile soil, full sun, and sustained warmth and humidity that all grafted durian require, and expect the multi-year wait to first fruiting typical of the species. Because the odor-reduction trait is the defining feature, orchardists sourcing this cultivar should confirm grafted material traces to the official breeding line rather than a seedling imitation.
sources: Department of Agriculture, Thailand — Durian Breeding Program (Songpol Somsri)

common_name: Khao Dawk Mali 105 Rice (Thai Jasmine Rice)

planting.note: Direct sow into flooded or consistently saturated ground after last frost once soil temperature reaches 65F; as a photoperiod-sensitive variety it will flower and mature in autumn regardless of exact sowing date.

directions: Khao Dawk Mali 105, the source variety behind Thai jasmine (hom mali) rice, traces to a single fragrant panicle selected near Ban Laem Pradu in Chonburi province, which was multiplied and officially registered under this name in the early 1950s. It is a tall, photoperiod-sensitive traditional variety grown as a single annual crop, concentrated today in the Thung Kula Rong Hai region of northeast Thailand where cool, dry-season nights help develop its signature aroma. The grain is slender and long, cooking up soft, slightly sticky, and faintly sweet, which has made it one of the world's most widely traded aromatic rice types. Grow it in saturated beds or shallow flood like other paddy rice, and harvest once the heads droop and turn golden-tan, then field-dry before hulling.
sources: Thailand Department of Agriculture — Rice Variety Registry
Rice Department, Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives (Thailand)
